name: Recurrent Hepatitis C Virus Induced Liver Disease in Liver Transplant Recipients

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Post-Transplant Hepatitis C Recurrence Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Detection of hepatitis C virus RNA in serum post-transplantation
Liver biopsy showing characteristic recurrent hepatitis C histopathology
Clinical signs of liver dysfunction including elevated transaminases and cholestasis
Exclusion of other causes of liver graft dysfunction such as rejection or drug toxicity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of detectable HCV RNA and histological evidence of recurrent hepatitis C in liver biopsy, with exclusion of other causes of graft dysfunction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of virological, histological, and clinical data post liver transplantation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Histological evidence of portal and lobular hepatitis with interface activity
searchTerms: liver inflammation with portal and lobular damage
histology showing hepatitis with interface activity

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic liver disease
searchTerms: fatigue related to chronic liver problems

common.notes: Detected on physical examination or imaging

occasional.notes: Itching related to bile salt accumulation
searchTerms: skin itching due to liver problems

occasional.notes: Yellow discoloration of skin and sclera

searchTerms: fluid buildup in abdomen from liver pressure

occasional.notes: Mild cognitive impairment due to liver dysfunction
searchTerms: mild to moderate brain dysfunction from liver failure
bleeding from enlarged veins due to portal hypertension
bleeding from swollen veins in liver disease

rare.symptomName: Severe hepatic fibrosis or cirrhosis progression

searchTerms: infection in belly fluid without surgery

laboratory: Positive HCV RNA by PCR in serum
Prolonged prothrombin time in advanced disease
imaging: Ultrasound showing hepatomegaly or nodular liver surface
Transient elastography indicating increased liver stiffness
other: Liver biopsy demonstrating recurrent hepatitis C histopathology with portal inflammation and interface hepatitis

distinguishingFeatures: Histology showing lymphocytic bile duct damage and endothelitis
Temporal relation to hepatotoxic drug exposure
Histology showing eosinophilic infiltration or cholestatic pattern

references: Forns X, et al. Recurrent hepatitis C after liver transplantation: natural history and treatment. J Hepatol. 2017.
Berenguer M. Natural history of recurrent hepatitis C. Liver Transpl. 2002.
Neumann UP, et al. Hepatitis C virus infection and liver transplantation. J Hepatol. 2019.
